purpose: Consolidate the completed bounded reviews for Ibn Kathir routes R01-R06, keeping route topology separate from proposition counting and authentication. All six routes now have protected source-level review artifacts; unresolved edition locators and the R05 textual divergence remain explicit.
controls: Independent collection records are not automatically independent historical witnesses.
Routes that converge at al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful are one lower-chain family despite different collection-level teachers.
A distinct chain with a different narrative setting supports only the meaning it actually states.
No external grading is adopted as QuranHikma's own judgment.
Narrator identity may be expanded only from an explicit parallel source-level witness; source transcriptions remain unexpanded.

explicit_disagreements_and_absences: R01: al-Nasa'i al-Kubra 11702 is directly verified; 11702/904/722 are numbering correspondences for one Ali ibn Hujr route.
R02 and R03: modern Musnad witnesses match the routes, but Ibn Kathir's 2/247 and 3/103 footnote pagination has not been reconciled to identified scans.
R04: Bukhari 4964 is an exact witness; checked Muslim 164a is related but not exact, so the printed Muslim attribution has no verified exact locator yet.
R05: the live/staged Ibn Hilal reading conflicts with public Ibn Kathir and al-Tabari Ibn Bilal; no repair is authorized without an identified edition scan.
R06: Sa'id is identified as Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah by an explicit parallel Yazid ibn Zuray' chain, but source transcriptions retain the abbreviated form.
No route review adopts an authentication grade, adds a proposition, changes the 73-claim count, or writes to the database.
The abridged English tafsir row is not used as a substitute for Arabic route text.
next_step: Move beyond the now-reviewed R01-R06 inventory: audit the complete Ibn Kathir route set and remaining edition/locator gaps, then select the next unresolved Surah 108 source issue without changing published claims.
